title: A ducat conformance vector file
description: One file of test vectors: provenance, then either cases (each with its own operation, arguments and expectation) or tables (rows of one operation's inputs and expected results). Every value is JSON text that needs no programming language to read: amounts are exact decimal strings, never JSON numbers. See spec/README.md for the meaning of each operation and expectation.

format.description: The version of this file format.

checkedAgainst.description: The ducat version (semver) whose TypeScript implementation passed every case in this file.

contentSha256.description: For a generated file whose generator stamps it: the SHA-256 of the cases' or rows' text as the generator wrote it, so an edit by hand is detected.

source.description: Where the expected values come from. Never from ducat's own output.

generator.description: The program that wrote the file, or null for values written by hand or copied from documentation.

tool.description: The program that computed the expected values, when it isn't the generator itself: LibreOffice Calc, or ICU.

data.description: The versions of reference data the expected values depend on.

runtimeIntl.description: Set when the results also depend on the runtime's own Intl or ICU data: what depends on it.

expectation.description: Exactly one key: what the operation must return, or the error it must raise, or any one of several alternatives.

decimal.description: An exact decimal: an optional minus sign, digits, and an optional fraction. No exponent, no plus sign.

money.description: An amount of money: the exact decimal amount, written with exactly `scale` fraction digits, its currency and its scale.

binary64.description: An IEEE 754 binary64 input: its shortest round-trip decimal form, and the exact decimal value of that double.

lcg.description: A linear congruential generator in exact integer arithmetic: state = (state * multiplier + increment) mod modulus, starting from seed.

draw.description: One draw from the generator: advance it once, then value = (state mod limit) + offset. With repeat, the draw is made as many times as the named earlier draw's value.

table.description: Rows of one table operation. Each row holds the operation's inputs and its expected results under the field names the operation defines (spec/README.md), so one row can check several results, such as one per rounding mode.

source.description: Where this table's rows come from, when that differs by table: a documentation page's URL, for instance.

parameters.description: Values that apply to every row of the table, such as the accuracy a documentation page states.

tableOp.description: A table operation; spec/README.md defines each one's row fields.

rowsByOp.description: The shape of each table operation's rows.

rational.description: An exact rational number: a decimal, or numerator/denominator with a positive denominator.

interval.description: An irrational result, given exactly: rationals lower and upper with lower <= value <= upper, and the tolerance an implementation's answer may differ from the true value by. exact is true when lower = upper is the value itself.

rate.description: A rate as the page's cell holds it: a decimal, or a decimal divided by an integer ("0.08/12").
A rate as the page's cell holds it: a decimal, or a decimal divided by an integer ("0.08/12").
A rate as the page's cell holds it: a decimal, or a decimal divided by an integer ("0.08/12").
A rate as the page's cell holds it: a decimal, or a decimal divided by an integer ("0.08/12").

spreadsheetNumber.description: A double as a spreadsheet prints it: 16 significant digits in scientific notation ("1.188443412335220E+03"), or an error ("Err:523", "#NUM!").

$comment: oneOf: a file has cases or tables, never both.
